issues.body: join_eq_r_repeated_pair_pads_and_accepts still calls two_pair_universe(), which commits A rows keyed by JK and JK2 and matching B rows for both keys. At slots A[2] x B[0], the committed graphs therefore have two genuine joined pairs, not the N=1 described by the test. Repeating the first pair validates repeated-lane padding, but the fixture does not validate that an actually one-match graph can fill R=2 lanes.
issues.fix_hint: Build JR2 from separately committed graphs with exactly one genuine joined pair, then repeat that sole pair across both lanes using distinct blinders. Keep JR1 on two_pair_universe() for the distinct-pair case.
issues.title: JR2 still claims N=1 while committing a two-match graph

verdict.summary: Round 5 is stagnant. The sole round-4 finding remains: JR2 still uses two_pair_universe(), whose committed graphs contain two genuine joined pairs at the selected slots, while the test says the prover holds only one genuine pair and labels the true cardinality N=1. Repeating the first pair does exercise lane reuse and fresh-blinder commitments, but it does not test the claimed one-match committed graph. The circuit relation and its limited cardinality claims otherwise remain consistent with the design.
